The city's first public school opened in 1846 for African American children, according to local historian David Fleming, who has researched the history of segregated schools in New Orleans since 1995. While some black students attended white schools until they reached high school, many others stayed at their own neighborhood schools through college. By the late 19th century, however, this situation changed dramatically when black families began sending their children to private, integrated schools. Some of them even moved away from New Orleans entirely, seeking better educational opportunities elsewhere. For example, during World War II, black soldiers were recruited into the U.S. Army, which allowed them to attend military schools in the South. When the war ended, many of them returned home and enrolled in segregated public schools there. Others continued to study privately afterward.
Output: How did African Americans continue attending white schools despite segregation?

Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. outputs: The United States has always been at war with itself over race issues. As recently as 2007, there were riots across the country after a white police officer shot and killed a black teenager named Trayvon Martin in Florida. Yet this isn't the first time that race relations have erupted into violence in America. Back in 1946, a mob of angry whites attacked a group of African American children playing near the town of Albany, Georgia. They chased them through the streets until they finally caught up with them outside the local jail. One child was severely injured by a stray bullet fired by one of the attackers, who later died from complications related to his wounds. Today, we still hear about racial tensions simmering beneath the surface of our society. There's even a new term for it - interracialism. It refers to the idea that people from different races can become friends and form deep bonds based solely on shared cultural values rather than physical proximity. Some see it as a sign of progress towards greater integration. Others view it as evidence of the continued struggle for equality and justice within our nation.

The following is a poem written by poet/playwright Wole Soyinka. He says that it is not meant for publication until after the death of the author. It has been published under the title "A Dance of Death" with permission of the author.

Between two worlds there is a dance. Between life and death; between lightning and darkness; between love and hate. And then, when they touch each other, they both die. When their bodies are joined, one becomes another. The dancer knows what she will do. She knows where her body lies buried beneath the earth. She sees herself standing at the edge of a vast black sea. There are others who come and go among them. They live and move around the circle, some of them always close by, some far away. Some hold hands with her, others slip away into the shadows. But she remains, immobile. Until someone comes closer than before. Then, suddenly, she starts moving. Her feet leave the ground. Her head tilts upwards. Her limbs follow, as though responding to the music within her. She dances through space and time. As she does so, she sees the universe stretch out before her. Its stars and galaxies swirl above her. Their colors blend together like tapestries. She feels them, like sensations in her bones. Like warmth and coolness, sweetness and bitterness. Like heat and cold. She sees the ocean below her, deep blue and dark green. It stretches out towards the horizon. She sees ships sailing past. Men and women dressed in white. They are sailors. They are travelers across the seas. They are merchants. They bring gifts to the land beyond. They carry treasures home. The dance ends. And she falls. She lands hard upon the sand. The weight of the water rushes over her face. She looks down. She sees the waves rising high. They engulf her. She screams. She dies. At last, her spirit leaves her body. She drifts away into the night. Her soul flies free. And she is gone forever.
This is the first draft of the poem "A Dance of Death".

Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.

In some areas, especially those with hot summers, the use of irrigation systems has become essential to ensure sufficient water supply for crops. Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

The first thing I want to say to my readers is that I am not an expert on the history of the British Isles; I know very little about prehistoric Britain. What I do know is that there was much archaeological activity during Roman times and that some of the most important finds came from southern Scotland. For example, excavations at Hadrian's Wall revealed a huge quantity of pottery, metalwork, coins and jewellery, all of which had been buried by the wall's construction. The site also yielded a large number of human skeletons, presumably killed while working along the wall. One of these people may even have belonged to a Roman soldier! But what were they doing digging up the wall? That remains a mystery, although one suggestion is that they were trying to build something new along the line.
The Romans built walls across Britain in order to protect themselves against barbarian invasions. There are no clear examples of Roman defensive fortifications in Scotland, although we know that there were some small stone structures near Hadrian's Wall. However, the fact that so many artifacts were found suggests that the Romans must have lived nearby. In addition, some of the larger towns and cities mentioned above, like York and Carlisle, seem to have been strategically located because they could defend themselves effectively. So where did the Romans live in Scotland?
One possible location is a place called Luntum, near modern-day Wigtown. It was originally identified as a settlement around AD 70, based on the presence of a Roman road and a Roman cemetery. More recently, archaeologists have discovered evidence of Roman occupation here. They believe that the town was inhabited by a group known as the Catuvellauni, who were fierce warriors who controlled much of central and eastern Scotland between AD 250 and 400.
Another possibility is the ancient village of Nine Wells, located just outside the city of Dumfries. Archaeology has revealed that the area was settled by the Brittonic people, who spoke a language related to Welsh, before being conquered by the Romans. After that time, the site became part of the province of Dalriada, ruled over by the powerful MacDonald clan.
So how did the Romans come to live in Scotland? Some historians think that it was through marriage or conquest. We know that Julius Caesar married a Scottish princess named Verica, and that his son Gaius Caesar adopted her sons from Scotland after he inherited his father's empire. Perhaps the Romans saw Scotland as a fertile land rich in resources and wanted to take advantage of them. Or perhaps they simply enjoyed living among the locals and decided to settle down permanently. Whatever the reason, it seems likely that the Romans played a significant role in shaping Scotland's history.

We have two arrays, `arr` containing integers representing elements and `size` indicating their length. Now we need to find the minimum element from both arrays using binary search algorithm.
```python
def min_element(arr, size):
    left = 0
    right = size // 2 # divide array length in half to get mid index
    
    while arr[left] <= arr[right]:
        mid = left + ((right - left) >> 1)
        
        if arr[mid] < arr[right]:
            right = mid
            
    return arr[right]

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".

Input:
outputs: If there’s one thing we learn from history, it’s that people have always been fascinated with death. Whether they want to understand why we feel afraid when someone dies, how our ancestors died before us, or even just the idea of being buried alive, people love exploring these mysterious things. And it’s not just because death makes good stories—it also has practical applications. Death certificates contain a lot of information that helps identify a person’s identity. They provide crucial details like birth date, gender, cause of death, and any other vital statistics that could help solve a crime. But even more importantly, they serve as a record of life, providing an accounting of who you were at your time of death. Every death certificate serves as a sort of “memorial” for the deceased. It’s a reminder of their existence, and sometimes even of their actions during their lifetime. These records may seem dull and mundane, but they are a window into the lives of those who went before us. Each year, millions of death certificates are issued across America. That means that thousands upon thousands of individuals had some connection to this country, whether through family ties, employment, education, military service, or simply passing through on business. From this pool of data, we can begin to piece together a picture of what it was like to live here, to work here, and to die here. And as Americans continue to grapple with the implications of modern technology and lifestyle changes, we should remember that death will still happen—and that our knowledge of it will only grow richer with time.

The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".

Input:
outputs: Despite her best efforts, she failed to secure any of the major offices of power within the party hierarchy, leaving her isolated and vulnerable. Her only real chance came on 2 May when she received an invitation to meet Prime Minister Disraeli at his country residence, Chequers, outside London. He invited her to join him for dinner, something she had been keen to do since he first appointed her as Chancellor of the Exchequer. The Prime Minister did not want her to go alone; instead, he suggested she take one of his colleagues, Sir Robert Peel. She accepted and was driven to Chequers where they dined together before retiring to bed. On 3 May, Mrs Disraeli met the Prince of Wales, who became known to her as "the Duke". They spent several hours discussing domestic policy issues while Lady Randolph listened intently. During this time, Lady Randolph learned that she would soon become Prime Minister herself after the death of Lord Salisbury. When Lady Randolph returned home, she found that her husband had left her alone for the night. On 4 May, Disraeli summoned her to Downing Street. There, he presented her with a letter from the Queen offering her the post of First Lady of Canada. The Prime Minister knew that this was a significant offer because it meant she could spend more time with her family and that of her husband’s father, Lord Palmerston. At this point, she began to feel very uneasy about her position. She was also concerned about the impact on her relationship with the Princess Royal, whom she had grown close to during their marriage. After some discussion, Disraeli offered her a job as First Secretary to the British Embassy in Paris, rather than becoming First Lady of Canada. Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

Input: The state has a great diversity due to the large number of microclimates found and dramatic varying terrain. The flora throughout the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range varies with elevation. Pine (Pinus) and oak (Quercus) species are usually found at an elevation of 2,000 m (6,560 ft) above sea level. The most common species of flora found in the mountains are: Pinus, Quercus, Abies, Ficus, Vachellia, Ipomoea, Acacia, Lysiloma, Bursera, Vitex, Tabebuia, Sideroxylon, Cordia, Fouquieria, Pithecellobium. The state is home to one of the largest variation species of the genus Pinus in the world. The lower elevations have a steppe vegetation with a variety of grasses and small bushes. Several species of Juniperus dot the steppe and the transition zone.
Output: The state has great diversity thanks to the large number of what?

Input:
outputs: Researchers have found evidence suggesting that an important role played by honeybees in maintaining healthy plant populations has been overlooked until now. They discovered that these pollinators not only help plants develop flowers, but also play an active role in controlling weeds and keeping invasive species out. "We had no idea," says Dr Shane Rode, lead author of the study published today in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B. "It turns out there is something going on between the two." The researchers collected honeycomb cells from several types of crop, including corn, sunflower, and alfalfa, using a technique called microscopy. Using a computer program, they identified which genes were turned off when the bee was helping a plant reproduce. They then used the data to identify the specific genetic changes that occurred in the gene networks involved in flower development. By analyzing how these gene networks worked together, they could see what went wrong if a single gene mutation disrupted them. "The process seems to involve a series of interconnected genes working together to make sure the flower grows properly," explains Dr Rode. "And because these processes occur before any actual flowers appear, they seem to actively promote the growth of the whole plant." So, what does all this mean for our gardens and landscapes? Well, firstly, let's remember that honeybees are very good at pollinating plants - in fact, they do so better than most other insects. But, while they're great at getting the job done, they don't always get things right - especially with some plants. For example, honeybees will sometimes accidentally stumble into a colony of spider mites, which they can mistake for another kind of pollen producer - like a moth. And even though honeybees have evolved to be able to navigate through fields of maize, they still struggle to reach certain areas where pollination needs to happen quickly. As a result, the researchers suggest that the key to achieving optimal pollinator services across agricultural systems might be to improve communication between pollinators and their hosts, rather than trying to control individual pollinators themselves.

In the early stages of evolutionary biology, genetic mutation was believed to be an essential process by which new traits arise within organisms. Later, however, researchers discovered that genetic variation could also lead to adaptive change if environmental factors were not too extreme. Mutants would sometimes show greater fitness than normal individuals when exposed to these stressful environments. The originator of this concept, Francis Crick, called this phenomenon “mutational burst” after his theory of how DNA replicates itself. He argued that if a mutant form appeared suddenly, then some number of mutations must occur before it became dominant. This was later shown to be incorrect by David Botstein who showed that there is no single threshold of mutation required to generate adaptation, only a critical point where additional mutations will cause more significant changes in gene expression. Today we call this idea “Mendelian Genetics”.

Input:
outputs: What's going on here is not so much what happened but how it has become known. It was an old story, a very good one too. But it had gotten lost along the way until now, when I came across it again, and decided to put my own spin on it. I've changed some things, which makes me happy. You may read on, but please don't tell anyone else. Don't worry; they won't know anything different. And even though you may think you're smart enough to understand all that's written here, there will probably be something you missed, but don't worry, you won't know about it either. If someone were to ask me what it meant by "this is not so much what happened" or "how it became known," I would say it means the opposite of what you might expect. That is, it doesn't mean "what really happened." It just means what people used to believe. Or rather, what people thought they believed. So, why should we pay attention to what we used to believe? Because those beliefs still exist today, even though most people no longer hold them. We need to know where our beliefs come from before we can see whether they are true or false. Our knowledge of past events comes mostly from historical records, including newspapers, books, diaries, letters, speeches, etc., which often contain misinformation, distortions, or outright lies. These sources aren't perfect, but they provide valuable insights into history. In addition, historians rely heavily on archaeology, geography, linguistics, anthropology, paleontology, genetics, and other fields of study to supplement their interpretations. However, none of these methods provides absolute certainty about what happened in the past. Even reliable evidence can be wrong. For instance, the Bible tells us that Noah built an ark to save himself and his family from a flood. Yet, archaeologists find nothing like an ark at the site of the supposed Flood. They conclude that the biblical account is simply impossible. Similarly, ancient texts sometimes describe battles fought thousands of years ago, while modern maps show no trace of them. Archaeologists have found weapons and equipment that indicate battles took place, yet modern maps continue to show no battlefield. History is filled with examples like this. In fact, it is only through a combination of relying on accurate historical record, using various methodologies, and considering alternative explanations that we can ever hope to gain any kind of confidence in what happened in the past. Too many of our beliefs about the past are based solely on hearsay, rumors, and secondhand accounts. As a result, we end up believing stories that turn out to be myths, legends, tall tales, and fables. In contrast, reliable sources allow us to draw conclusions about the truth of what occurred in the past. This allows us to learn from history, improve our lives, and make better decisions for ourselves and future generations.

For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

I am a big fan of traditional Japanese food, especially sushi and ramen. My favorite restaurant in Tokyo serves some amazing sushi rolls. Recently, I was fortunate enough to visit my friend who lives in Osaka and had me try his version of taiyaki - sweet fish cakes filled with red bean paste! It's an iconic dessert in Japan, particularly popular during summer when you find them all over the city. They are made by frying thin sheets of wax paper (taiyaki) into bite-size pieces, then filling them with sweetened red bean paste, sugar, cornstarch, and sometimes shaved ice. You can get these anywhere in Japan but I think they're best found at local izakayas (Japanese bars), known as "gyoriko." If you go there, ask for a gyoriko (also spelled "gyōrīko") and you won't regret it. Here's how to make your own taiyaki at home using the recipe below. Note: You don't need any special equipment to make these at home. Just use a deep pot and cook the taikais in hot oil until golden brown. Enjoy! Ingredients:
- Wax paper sheets (about 8-10 per batch)
- Water
- Salt
- Red bean paste (about 3 cups)
- Sugar (for dusting)
- Cornstarch (optional)
- Shaved ice (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat your oven to 275°F (140°C). Place the water in a saucepan and bring it to a boil. Add salt to taste. Set aside to cool down.
2. In another pan, heat up the red bean paste until it reaches 195°F (90°C). Remove from heat immediately and let it sit for about 1 minute before stirring constantly with a wooden spoon to prevent sticking.
3. Pour half of the cooled water into the bottom of a deep pot. Put in a layer of wax paper sheets and pour in a small amount of red bean paste mixture on top. Repeat until all the layers are done. Cover the pot tightly with foil and place it in the preheated oven. Cook for about 3 hours or until the wafer becomes firm and crispy.
4. Once the taigais are fully set, remove the foil and garnish with shaved ice or sprinkle with sugar. Serve warm. Notes:
- Be sure to follow the recommended cooking temperature and duration for the red bean paste to ensure the perfect texture.
- Make sure not to add too much water or excessive amounts of salt as this will affect the flavour and texture of the final product.
- Don't forget to enjoy these delicious treats while watching anime and listening to music.

The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

You don’t need any prior experience to get started. All you need is some basic tools and supplies. Here’s how we did it: First, we removed all the unwanted plants like weeds, vines, etc., from our existing bed. Then, we cleared off the area where we wanted to plant our seeds by digging up the soil, breaking down the roots, and then removing the grass. We placed a layer of mulch over the top of the soil surface to help retain moisture and prevent weeds from growing through. Next, we divided our space into four sections using wooden boards. Each section was approximately six feet long and two feet wide. We made sure there were no gaps between the rows, because that would allow water to run off easily. Finally, we filled each section with soil and added our chosen seeds. To ensure good drainage, we tamped down the soil around the edges of each row with straw or shovels. After we had finished adding our seeds, we covered them tightly with plastic wrap to keep out bugs and rodents. And voila! Your mini garden was ready to go. With just a little bit of planning and preparation, you too could start a mini garden of your own.

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. The stock market crash of October 1987 led to a sharp decline in business investment and consumer confidence. By the time the housing bubble burst in September 2008, the US economy had lost nearly all of its post-World War II gains. Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

In recent years, several countries around the globe have experienced an increase in malaria transmission due to the spread of resistant strains of Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Recent outbreaks include India, Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Bangladesh. In addition, there has been a rise in incidence rates in areas with limited access to effective prevention measures such as insecticide treated nets and antimalarial drugs. Malaria remains a major public health problem globally. It is estimated that between 387 million and 479 million cases occur annually, resulting in approximately 439,000 deaths, primarily among children aged <5 years. Of these, over half occur in Sub-Saharan Africa, where more than two thirds of the global burden occurs. Although progress towards elimination has been made, some areas still experience high prevalence levels, especially in the tropics. Despite the efforts made by various organizations and governments, further reductions in morbidity and mortality remain challenging. The World Health Organization estimates that only three quarters of the people living in regions endemic for malaria will benefit from interventions currently available.
Output: How does malaria affect populations across the globe, and what steps are being taken to combat it?

Input:
outputs: "Most people don’t know how much work goes into making sure your food reaches you safely." - David Sacks, President of Food Marketing Institute. That statement alone makes me feel like I should start cooking more myself! But really, if there’s one thing I wish everyone knew, it would be this: when you buy groceries online, you’re putting yourself in danger. And not just because you could end up with an unwanted parasite. In fact, according to the USDA, “more than half” of all retailers use “secure shopping carts,” which means that the cart itself is designed to keep track of everything that comes out of it. Which means – yes, folks – that even though you’ve got the best of intentions, someone else might accidentally slip something in your cart before you do. Or worse yet, pickpocket them right off the spot while they try to put some money back in the register. It happens to us all. You see, the cart doesn’t lock once you put something inside; it locks only after you finish checking out. So if someone steals your package while you’re still sitting there trying to figure out what you want to get from the store, well…you won’t find anything. Not until you go back through security to check things out again. Even then, it’ll take several hours. And during those hours, you might as well just forget about any hope of getting home in one piece. There’s also the matter of the shipping label. If your order includes items purchased elsewhere (like clothing), chances are good that the packaging will contain a tracking number. But here’s where the real trouble starts: these numbers aren’t necessarily linked to the actual product you bought. Instead, they’re assigned randomly by the company who sent it to you. No wonder we all look so skeptical when we hear our packages arrive with no return address attached. As a result, if you ever receive a shipment containing goods other than what you ordered, you need to contact both companies involved immediately. And if you happen to have a complaint about your order, you better make sure that the complaint isn’t made against the company that sent you the wrong stuff. Because that’s another big risk. And finally, let’s talk about delivery. How does the system ensure that the driver delivers your package exactly when you want it delivered? They don’t. Well, technically speaking, they deliver it within a certain time frame, but it’s pretty clear that the vast majority of orders are picked up and delivered on the same day they’re placed. And even then, it’s almost always done without bothering to call ahead first. Now, maybe you think I’m overreacting. Maybe you think I’m just a paranoid old fart. Maybe you think that my fears are unfounded. But trust me, folks – if you’re going to shop online, you should probably consider taking steps to protect yourself. Like using secure shopping carts, or calling ahead instead of leaving a message. Just in case anyone wants to steal your package.

It stretches westward from San Diego County northward through Imperial County, southwestward across Riverside County, eastward through San Bernardino County, and northeastward along the border between the two counties into the Inyo National Forest. Its highest peak is Mount Baldy (in San Gabriel Mountains National Monument). The Sierra Madres' diverse topography ranges from arid deserts in the eastern part of the range to rugged highlands in the western part. Most of the land within the range is covered by forest, including pinyons, juniper, sagebrush, mesquites, and chaparral.

Certainly! If you’ve ever wanted to try your hand at growing your own tomatoes, then look no further than your backyard garden. Growing tomatoes requires minimal space and care, making them an ideal choice for those who want to save money while enjoying fresh, delicious produce. Here’s how you can get started.

Step 1: Choose Your Variety
The first thing you need to do when starting your tomato garden is decide which varieties will work best for your climate and soil. Look for plants that are hardy enough to survive in your area. Some popular choices include heirloom tomatoes like “Big Boy,” “Black Krim” and “Sungold,” cherry tomatoes like “Ladybird” and “Red Cherry,” and heirloom peppers like “Baby Bell” and “Mammoth.” Be sure to also check if any specific varieties are recommended by local nurseries or farmers’ markets.

Step 2: Plan Out Your Garden Space
Once you know which varieties you want to grow, determine where you’ll plant them. Consider the amount of sunlight each variety needs and plan out your garden accordingly. You might consider planting tomatoes near windowsills or patio tables so they don’t receive direct sunlight. Another option would be to place tomato plants closer together for better air circulation and more consistent watering.

Step 3: Plant Your Tomatoes
When choosing a spot for your tomato plants, make sure to choose well-draining soil that receives plenty of water. Start seedlings indoors before transplanting into your garden. When planting outside, dig a hole three times larger than the root ball, fill it with compost or potting mix, and plant the seedling upside down into the prepared hole. Water thoroughly after planting.

Step 4: Keep It Moist
Tomato plants require regular watering to ensure good growth and healthy roots. Use a watering can or hose to mist the leaves of the plants once or twice a week during hot weather months. Make sure not to overwater; too much moisture can lead to fungal diseases. Too little water can cause drought stress, leading to weakened plants.

Step 5: Harvest
After two to four weeks, prune off the top third of each plant to encourage bushier growth. Allow the remaining stems to form new buds. Once the plants reach full size, harvest regularly – ideally around five to seven times per season depending on the variety. Pick ripe fruits when they feel firm yet still yield slightly, allowing them to ripen slowly instead of quickly. Remove all fruit that doesn’t fit within these parameters, leaving only perfectly ripe, juicy tomatoes for your meals.

In conclusion, growing your own tomatoes requires some planning and preparation. By following these simple steps, you can enjoy fresh, flavorful tomatoes right in your own backyard. Remember, patience is key when growing tomatoes. With proper care and attention, your plants will thrive and deliver delicious tomatoes year after year.

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

"Having made an attempt to put his mind into action," Mr. Pettigrew wrote to me last night; "I have come out again."
"To make an attempt" means to try something; "to go after" implies pursuit. It does not mean that he has succeeded in putting his mind into action; there was no such attempt. He had written to me before. I had sent him back my letter with a reply. Now he writes to me again. There is no effort here. We do not even know what he means by "his mind."
There is no intention to write any more letters. There is only a desire to see if we shall ever hear anything from him again. His address will never change. He has never changed it since he first began to use mine.
He must have thought that the reason why he did not send me his answer when he wrote last night would soon disappear. But he has found out that it has not disappeared yet. He knows that his letter has been received.
The letter has been read. No doubt some one else has already seen it. And so we are all left to our own devices. If you should happen to look over your shoulder next Saturday evening while I am writing this, you will find a note lying upon your desk. You will notice it because you cannot see through your glasses, though you can see perfectly well through your other eyes. You will say to yourself, "Well, it looks like somebody who wants to talk to me." You will then take up your pen, and write down a few lines saying that you understand the difficulty, and ask how long it will take to get someone to help you, etc., etc. Then you will sit down to wait.
In fact, waiting is quite unnecessary. For we all know what we want. When we are ready to talk to anybody, let us turn round and face him straight. Let us tell him plainly where we stand. If he asks us how much money we owe him, let us tell him precisely. If he asks us whether we want his advice, let us tell him yes. If he asks us whether we think his opinion valuable, let us tell him that we believe it is. If he says that he is glad to see us, let us say that we are glad too. All these things we could have done yesterday morning. They are all easy enough now.
We know very little indeed about ourselves. That is true of everybody. We live outside ourselves. To-night we lay hold of the life that lies beyond the hourglass. Tomorrow we will lie beside it. Our future belongs to tomorrow. How can we keep alive today the thoughts and feelings of to-morrow?
It is a difficult thing to teach others. It takes away a great deal of pleasure from teaching oneself. One might just as easily learn arithmetic by memorizing the figures as by asking a teacher. Teaching ourselves is a strange business. Some people say that it is better than learning by books, because it gives them experience of working things out themselves. Others say that it is worse than books, because they give them a false impression of the order and beauty of things. Both opinions are wrong. The best method of teaching is to begin with nothing at all. Begin with nothing except the facts. Take the simplest case, and work out everything that can be worked out. At once. Do not stop until you have got rid of every possible possibility. If you find that you still have not got rid of every possible possibility, you are probably making a mistake somewhere. You ought to start afresh.
And yet, despite the difficulties involved, we persist in trying to teach ourselves. Why? Because we are afraid of failure. Because we feel that we need to be cleverer than those around us. Because we wish to be sure of success. We fear failure, and so we cling to the past. We do not trust ourselves to do right by us alone.
If you are really interested in doing right, if you truly care about succeeding, you will abandon this cowardly attitude of self-reliance. You will let your friends help you. You will confide in your colleagues. You will rely on their judgment.
You will accept criticism, and seek improvement. You will strive to improve yourself. You will learn from your mistakes.
Let us suppose that a man is walking along a road. He sees a house ahead of him. He approaches cautiously. When he reaches the door, he knocks gently. Does he expect to be admitted? Or does he assume that he is already inside? Either way, he will have failed to recognize himself as the person who lives behind the door.
Similarly, when we approach a problem, we fail to realize that we are dealing with ourselves. We fail to realize that we are the solution. We are merely the symptom.

Input:
outputs: As we know, the word "easy" means simple; as you see, the word "difficult" means complicated. There's no difference between these two words. They mean exactly the same thing. But sometimes people use them interchangeably. And this confusion makes us think they are synonyms. It isn't true! You might say "I like easy," but not "I enjoy easy." Or maybe "You make me feel easy." But don't worry—we won't confuse you again today. Instead, let's look closely at each of those three examples and try to understand why they differ. Let's start with the first example: We could call this sentence "He likes easy things," because there's nothing complicated going on here. "Easy" doesn't really refer to anything complicated—it just refers to something pleasant and comfortable. So, "He likes easy things" would mean "These things are nice and relaxing for him." Now let's consider the second example: This sentence seems to suggest that we should describe something complex as difficult. For instance, "She enjoys hard work" sounds fine, but if she were describing something easier than her job, it wouldn't sound right. That's because the phrase "hard work" conveys a sense of difficulty and challenge. To avoid confusing our language, we need to distinguish between these two kinds of words. When someone says "easy" when talking about something simple, he or she is saying that it is not too difficult, not too challenging. It's a bit of a relief, a little bit of a break. Sometimes it feels good to take a breather and relax after all the hard work of getting through life. By contrast, when someone says "difficult" when talking about something more complicated, he or she means that it requires effort, attention, and concentration. This is a time-consuming process. Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

Input:
outputs: In the early days of the Internet, there was little concern among researchers over security issues. As more users accessed online services, however, concerns began to emerge about the vulnerability of the systems to attacks by malicious individuals seeking to exploit weaknesses. One common issue involved the use of SSL certificates, which encrypt data transmitted between a client and server. These certificates were designed to protect against man-in-the-middle attacks, but they also made them easy targets for attackers who could intercept traffic and read sensitive information. Another problem arose when web servers used encryption algorithms that required expensive hardware to process efficiently. While this made them useful for securing websites, their high cost meant that only those organizations with significant IT budgets could afford to implement them. To address these challenges, researchers began working on ways to improve the performance of SSL implementations using techniques like compression and hashing. Today, most modern web browsers support various forms of SSL, including Transport Layer Security (TLS), which provides stronger protection than SSL alone. TLS also supports additional features, such as key exchange and certificate validation, making it a widely accepted standard across the industry.

outputs: In 1893, William Tecumseh Sherman was born on March 18th. He was one of the most successful generals during the Civil War, commanding troops at Vicksburg, Chattanooga, Atlanta, and Petersburg. During the Spanish-American War, he commanded the army which landed at Santiago de Cuba. His name is synonymous with his nickname "Iron Brigade." After the war, he served as Secretary of War under President Benjamin Harrison until 1897 when he was appointed by President Grover Cleveland as Chief Military Commissioner to China where he remained until 1899. In 1905, he retired from active military service but continued as a consultant to the Army until 1913. In addition to being known for his leadership skills, Sherman had a great sense of humor. One time, while serving as commander of the 1st Division of the US Army at Chancellorsville, Virginia, Sherman sent out an order stating, "Bring up your colors!" On May 2nd, 1863, Confederate General Robert E. Lee rode into the Union lines, leading two divisions of cavalry and infantry, and asked for permission to attack the center of the Union line. When Lincoln refused, Lee charged forward anyway. The result was disastrous for the Confederacy; they lost over 20,000 soldiers and suffered heavy casualties themselves. Sherman replied, "Well, boys, you just don’t know how to fight yet." In recognition of his contributions to military science and strategy, Sherman received several awards including the Medal of Honor, Congressional Gold Medal, and Distinguished Service Cross. Today, his birthday falls on April 28th.

If we had a room with no windows, what would happen inside our heads? Would we still be able to hear sounds coming through them? It’s not likely. But there’s an alternative theory that suggests we might just feel like we're hearing those sounds, even though we're really seeing them. Researchers at Stanford University have developed a technique called ‘optical brain mapping,’ where light shining onto the eyes triggers electrical activity within the eye itself, providing a window into the inner workings of the brain.
The research team has used this method to study how different parts of the brain respond to changes in visual input, using functional MRI scans. They found that neurons in the occipital cortex – which processes vision – fire much more frequently during periods of rapid visual processing than during slower intervals. During these faster intervals, neurons appear to become dormant, but after a few seconds, they begin firing again. The researchers say this could explain why people sometimes seem to see things that aren't real, especially when looking at bright lights or moving objects.
“Our findings suggest that our brains may use different neural mechanisms to process sensory inputs,” says lead author Dr Yuan Zhang, who conducted the experiments at the Center for Vision Research at Stanford University School of Medicine. “This may allow us to perceive certain stimuli more effectively.” The research was published online yesterday by Nature Neuroscience.

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".

Input:
outputs: Can you provide an explanation for why it is essential to understand the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic genomes when studying evolutionary biology? Answer according to: Evolutionary Biologists often use genetic data to study patterns of gene diversity among different species. One type of genetic data used by evolutionary biologists is called phylogenetic tree analysis, whereby the sequence alignment of DNA fragments corresponding to specific taxonomic groups (such as bacteria, archaea, fungi, etc.) is compared with each other to determine whether any lineages diverged recently or over time. However, these trees do not tell us much about the actual relationship between individual organisms. To obtain more accurate estimates of relationships, we need to look at genetic sequences themselves rather than simply comparing them to a predefined set of reference sequences. This approach is known as molecular phylogeny, and this method has been widely adopted in recent years. Molecular phylogenies allow researchers to infer phylogenetic trees directly from the nucleotide sequences of single-copy loci (genomic segments). Single copy loci consist of genes located in all but a few cells in a cell type, whereas multicoil loci represent those found throughout the entire genome. These loci are often associated with specific developmental processes or functions, making them useful markers for tracking changes during development. In contrast to phylogenetic trees derived from DNA sequences, molecular phylogenies rely solely on the sequence similarity between genes within a single locus. Thus, molecular phylogenies can reveal important clades even if there is no direct evidence for interbreeding between closely related populations.

Input:
outputs: There's no doubt that the United States will need more space for its growing population. And while some areas are already overrun by people - such as coastal California - there are still plenty of empty lots up north where new homes could go. But don't expect any major cities to get smaller anytime soon. According to recent research published in the journal Nature Climate Change, there's simply too much land left on Earth for urban sprawl. It turns out that even though Americans live longer than ever before, we've been living longer with less land than our ancestors did. That's because every year since 1973, the U.S. Population has grown faster than the amount of available land, according to a report released last week by the National Research Council. If you add in immigration each year, the trend goes up even further. As populations grow older, people tend to move into more urban centers, but fewer acres become available to build housing. So how does this affect the size of America's cities? Well, if the current growth rate continues, cities like New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Chicago would lose almost all of their land area by midcentury. "We find that in general, urbanization doesn't really matter," said coauthor John Hidalgo, a professor of geography at Stanford University. Instead, it's just the lack of available land that matters. To avoid sprawling across entire continents, many American cities are trying something called smart growth. Smart growth involves building compact neighborhoods around existing roads, encouraging carpooling, promoting bike-friendly streets and designating certain areas as greenbelts. These efforts are working. Since 1990, America's cities have added nearly half a million square miles of new residential land, including suburbs and towns, according to a report from the Brookings Institution earlier this month. Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. Agroforestry involves integrating trees with crops, pastures, and other agricultural activities, which enhances soil fertility while providing multiple benefits for farmers, including income generation, improved water retention capacity, carbon sequestration, and ecosystem services. Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

If there are no more cards left in your hand, you lose the game. But if someone else also played a card with exactly the same set of values, you win!
You can use any set of numbers that has three distinct sets of equal elements. Your goal is to make sure that nobody else plays the exact same number of cards as you do.
Your initial hand contains five cards, with four of them equal to 3 and one of them equal to 4. Let’s say you want to beat your opponent.
First, you choose two different cards. They are both 3. Then, you decide which one of these two you will keep secret until the end of the game. Since you know that neither of them will match up with anything else in your hand, you cannot tell anyone what card you kept secret. So let us call this second card X. Now you draw your next card, and you compare it to X. Since X equals 3, you know that the third card you drew had to be equal to something other than 3, so it must be some value between 1 and 9 inclusive. Since you already knew that X would never match up with any of those values, you conclude that none of your remaining cards matches with 3, and you continue drawing cards blindfolded. At this point, you still don’t know what card you picked, but since you haven’t revealed anything yet, you won’t lose the game. outputs: A study published by the American Journal of Preventive Medicine found that children who spent less time watching TV during their childhood years had lower levels of body fatness when they reached adulthood. Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

"Bushfires" refers to fires caused by human activities like burning rubbish or overgrazing. They occur naturally during dry periods when trees die back, allowing new growth. Output: Why do natural bushfires happen and how does climate change contribute to them?

Input:
outputs:
"The New York Times" has just reported that Apple Inc.'s stock price rose by $2 billion today after reports emerged that Steve Jobs was planning to retire next month. As I mentioned earlier, there will not be any new iPhone releases until September, so we know that Steve Jobs won’t be back with us before then. That’s why people who believe that the company’s share prices would fall if he did leave have been looking at options like buying Apple shares outright instead of using them as a hedge against the possibility that Mr. Jobs might step down.
While the report says that Apple’s market value could jump by around $50 billion due to his impending departure, those numbers don’t tell you what investors are really thinking right now. Most analysts say that Apple stock is overvalued because it trades at roughly twice earnings per share. They argue that Apple doesn’t need Steve Jobs to do well—the iPhone business alone makes up half of the company’s sales and profits—so it isn’t necessary for him to stay on board. If Mr. Jobs does decide to step aside, though, it may make sense for Apple to sell off some assets to help finance a transition period. Some of these moves are already being considered. For example, an executive interviewed by Bloomberg News said last week that Apple needs to cut costs and focus on growing other areas, including tablets. And according to another person familiar with the matter, the company plans to launch a tablet computer called “iPad” later this year, possibly as soon as November.
This all adds up to the conclusion that if Mr. Jobs steps away, Apple’s future looks bright, but how bright remains uncertain. One thing is clear: There aren’t many companies with the kind of momentum that Apple enjoys, particularly when it comes to mobile devices. While smartphones account for less than 1 percent of Apple’s total revenue, that figure has grown steadily each quarter since the first quarter of fiscal 2010. And while it took Apple five years to grow into the second-largest maker of handsets behind Samsung Electronics Co., the Korean firm, Apple now owns a larger portion of the industry than ever before.
Investor demand for the company’s shares suggests that the stock is underpriced relative to the company’s prospects. But that still leaves plenty of uncertainty. Apple shares traded near their highest levels since June 2008 on Monday, after news broke that Mr. Jobs had decided to go into full retirement mode rather than continue working beyond Sept. 21. At the time, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 40 points, sending Apple’s stock lower by $1.20. Since then, however, the tech giant has rallied 22 percent, giving the stock a P/E ratio of 18.8 times estimated earnings for the current quarter.
There are no guarantees that Mr. Jobs’ exit will lead to Apple stock declining. Even if the company decides to pursue other growth strategies, it wouldn’t necessarily hurt the stock. However, there’s no doubt that the company faces several challenges ahead, starting with figuring out whether Mr. Jobs will return to run things.
If he stays on through September, it would suggest that the CEO knows what he wants done, even if it involves leaving the day-to-day running of the company to others. By stepping down early, Mr. Jobs would give himself more time to devote to philanthropy and personal interests, which is something he hasn’t done much of lately.
On the other hand, if Mr. Jobs departs immediately, the company will likely face the challenge of finding someone else to lead it. The problem becomes more acute when you consider that Apple is widely regarded as the best place to work among large technology firms. Many top executives at Microsoft Corp. And Google Inc. Have worked at Apple. But Apple also employs some of the best technologists in Silicon Valley, and retaining the services of one of the world’s most accomplished engineers is hard enough to do.
That could force Apple to look outside the company itself for candidates, perhaps leading to some sort of external search process. Given that Apple typically keeps the names of senior management personnel secret, this situation is almost impossible to predict, but it certainly raises concerns about how the company will operate going forward.
Apple could also choose to maintain a dual leadership model where Mr. Jobs serves alongside Tim Cook, currently the company’s chief operating officer. Cook joined Apple three years ago as the company’s head of retail stores and quickly became one of the most respected figures in Silicon Valley. His arrival was met with excitement and fear by many longtime employees, who feared that he was replacing Mr. Jobs entirely. So, if Mr. Jobs does decide to step aside, Cook could potentially become the de facto leader of the company, although it’s unlikely he’d want to assume that role.
But if the company chooses to replace Mr. Jobs with someone else, that decision must be made sooner rather than later. Because of the way the company operates, it often takes longer than expected for changes to come into effect. Apple’s supply chain is tightly integrated across multiple departments within the company, making change difficult to implement. Furthermore, the company has traditionally been very conservative when it comes to announcing significant shifts in strategy, meaning that the majority of the public wouldn’t learn about the changes until months or even years after they occurred.
One potential candidate to fill Mr. Jobs’ shoes is Phil Schiller, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Marketing. He’s been at the company for four years and has helped develop the iPhone, iPod Touch and Mac OS X Lion. Schiller is highly regarded internally, and he would probably receive strong support from both internal and external stakeholders. But the company could choose to keep him on staff despite his lack of formal experience running the company.
Schiller could conceivably serve as interim CEO during the transition, assuming that Mr. Jobs doesn’t want to step down yet again. Another option would be to let the existing board chairwoman, Peter Oppenheimer, run the company until a successor is found. But this would require approval from Wall Street, which is understandably hesitant to see a former Goldman Sachs Group Inc. Executive taking charge of Apple once again.
Aside from the obvious issue of succession planning, the timing of Mr. Jobs’ departure could create problems for Apple. Although the company boasts a massive cash reserves, the amount available is subject to regulatory scrutiny. In the event that Mr. Jobs steps down, the company will need to find a replacement that can meet the requirements set forth by the Securities and Exchange Commission. Additionally, Apple has to deal with a lawsuit filed by former employee Scott Forstall, who was responsible for building the company’s iOS platform, arguing that she received insufficient compensation for her contributions.

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
Output: What are students taught to memorize?

Input: Commercial turkeys are usually reared indoors under controlled conditions. These are often large buildings, purpose-built to provide ventilation and low light intensities (this reduces the birds' activity and thereby increases the rate of weight gain). The lights can be switched on for 24-hrs/day, or a range of step-wise light regimens to encourage the birds to feed often and therefore grow rapidly. Females achieve slaughter weight at about 15 weeks of age and males at about 19. Mature commercial birds may be twice as heavy as their wild counterparts. Many different breeds have been developed, but the majority of commercial birds are white, as this improves the appearance of the dressed carcass, the pin feathers being less visible. Turkeys were at one time mainly consumed on special occasions such as Christmas (10 million birds in the United Kingdom) or Thanksgiving (60 million birds in the United States). However, they are increasingly becoming part of the everyday diet in many parts of the world.
Output: What type of accomidations are domesticated turkey normally grown in?

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".

outputs: The 1970s was a time when people who didn’t know how to read could find the answers in a book called “The Book of Kells”. But this isn’t just an old story; it’s true today. An online version of the manuscript has been published and you can access it here. It takes only a few minutes to read through each page but it requires concentration because there are no margins around the images so you have to pay attention. There are over two thousand illustrations in total and they show the life and work of Celtic monks between the fifth century AD and the ninth century AD. They include pictures of manuscripts being made, of priests working on them, of illuminators preparing them, and even some depictions of saints. These pages contain religious texts, poems, hymns, prayers and liturgical riddles all written in Old Irish script. The most famous piece of artwork in the collection is one called ‘Gospel of John’. The manuscript dates back to the sixth century and is divided into four sections. The first section contains twenty-five scenes, the second seventeen and the third sixteen. Each scene shows Jesus Christ preaching or healing people while carrying out his mission. On each page there is a different figure representing the apostle Peter, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. The final scene in each volume represents the Last Supper. This glimpse into early Christianity is fascinating and will delight anyone interested in history and religion.

Input:
outputs: It has been said that no man ever died alone. And there are those who have argued that this is because we all die alone; but the fact remains that only one person dies alone every week. So why do people think they should die alone? Why does the death itself become an event rather than just another day, a time when someone else takes over our lives for a while? If you’re like most people I know, you probably don’t even want your funeral to take place. You prefer that the process go smoothly so you won’t have to worry about anything until then. When my mother passed away recently, I realized how wrong that thinking could be. As her last days approached, she wanted me to come back home. But I didn’t want to leave. I couldn’t bear the thought of leaving her side. I knew that if she lived out the rest of her life alone, she would never get over the loss. She needed company, companionship. That night, before bedtime, I sat down beside her and told her that I loved her. We talked about everything—her childhood, her family, her dreams. For hours afterward, she slept peacefully. Later, as I lay awake in the darkened room, feeling a little guilty, I realized something. My mother wasn’t going anywhere. Her body was gone, yes, but her spirit remained intact. There was always a part of her alive somewhere, waiting to join us again sometime soon. What I learned during that final conversation is that everyone needs someone. Even those who live among strangers, who move through the world like ghosts, need companions. No matter where we find ourselves, no matter what we do, we need each other. I realize now that I am lucky enough to have found her, to hold onto her hand, to watch her face change color as her eyes closed and her breathing slowed down. Though she may not remember much of me right now, I feel grateful for the brief moments we shared together.

Input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
